| **Summary** | Journal-hosted submission page (thejap.org) confirms authors must disclose AI use "when technologies have made a substantive contribution to the development, organization, or writing of the work" — this mirrors Wiley's generic publisher-wide Generative AI Guidelines for Authors (permitted for language/grammar/idea development/lit search/coding assistance with mandatory disclosure; prohibited for authorship credit, image/data fabrication, or unverified drafting of results/conclusions/abstracts). No JAP-specific AI policy page distinct from the Wiley boilerplate was found — the thejap.org text appears to restate Wiley's standard policy rather than add journal-specific restrictions. |
| **Source URL** | https://thejap.org/resources/submit-an-article |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes, under Wiley's publisher-wide policy (no JAP-specific preprint page found): authors may self-archive/post the submitted preprint version at any time on non-commercial preprint servers, no need to remove before or during submission; accepted (peer-reviewed) version can be self-archived after embargo (Wiley standard: 24 months for SSH-classified journals, which JAP likely falls under as a psychoanalysis/humanities-adjacent journal, though this classification was not directly confirmed for JAP itself).
> Source: https://authors.wiley.com/author-resources/Journal-Authors/open-access/preprints-policy.html

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Clinical/case-based Jungian analytic papers, theoretical papers on analytical psychology, and papers engaging archetypal/cultural themes. Example 2025 items: "Emotional Intelligence and Transformation in Analytical Psychology: A Case Study" (Pellitteri, Vol 70 Issue 2, Feb 2025); a September 2025 special issue titled "War: Archetypal Energies, Cultural Discontent, Internal Discord" indicates current editorial appetite for archetypal analysis of contemporary geopolitical/cultural trauma. Journal published 5x/year (Feb, Apr, Jun, Sep, Nov).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** single/multiple clinical case studies, theoretical/conceptual papers on Jungian analytic theory, archetypal-cultural analysis (e.g., war, collective trauma), book and journal reviews
